findings.issue: SPEC-03 uses a hand-rolled try/catch plus two expects where a single Vitest matcher would do.
findings.evidence: let thrown: unknown; try { chartCell(...) } catch (error) { thrown = error; } expect(thrown).toBeInstanceOf(RangeError); expect(message).toBe(...)
findings.fix: Optional: expect(() => chartCell(chart, 'CO', 'unopened', hc)).toThrow(new RangeError(`Unknown hand class ${hc}`)) together with a toThrow(RangeError) check; the current form is correct and fails when the behaviour breaks.

summary: The diff matches the spec exactly. The module-private echo() with ECHO_CHARS = 20 is used at the three specified sites (invalid action, invalid alternative, spot does not apply). The chartCell JSDoc lists both RangeErrors, and no other behaviour changes. The tests would catch a broken implementation: the /\S+/ wordCount mutant counts 60 tokens, so both SPEC-01 asserts fail. Off-by-one mutants (< in place of <=, or a limit of 19 or 21) fail the exact-20 and 31-character cases in SPEC-04/05. Removing echo at any site fails its exact-string assert. A missing throw or wrong message fails SPEC-03. Only the two specified files changed. The 153 changed lines exceed the 130-line budget, which is a warning only, because the spec told the builder to copy the test helpers. Gates pass (test, lint, typecheck), and the new test file passes on its own (5/5).
